title: Establish preemptive error-budget runway & staged circuit-breaker spec for endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: We currently react to SLO breaches after burn events; this leads to noisy failovers and customer-visible degradations. We need a preemptive "runway" model that watches short- and medium-term burn trajectories and triggers staged circuit-breakers and load-shedding actions before full SLO collapse. Goal: define SLI formulas, runway windows, burn-rate thresholds, staged breaker actions, and telemetry/dashboards; implement a policy engine hookpoints for runtime to enact actions (restrict, degrade, regional-eject). This ticket defines the spec, runbook, and acceptance criteria for platform and runtime teams.
context: Scope: per-endpoint and per-model SLO/SLI runway definitions; interactions with model variants, KV-cache impact, and multi-region failover. Not in scope: billing changes or customer UI for manual override (will be follow-ups).
deliverables: Burn-rate bands and mapping to staged actions: Notice / Throttle / Evacuate
Circuit-breaker state machine and hysteresis rules
Load-shedding priority ladder (by tenant weight, route, model variant)
Test plan + loadtest harness scenarios and PR for runtime hookpoints
decision_rationale: We chose a runway-first model because short spikes can vaporize error budgets quickly; by modeling the burn trajectory we can act earlier with lower customer impact. Staged actions preserve highest-value traffic (pinned variants, enterprise SLA tokens) while shedding opportunistic, low-value requests. Hysteresis and lane-specific thresholds reduce flip-flopping during noisy signals.
sli_definitions: availability_sli: successful-response-rate over 1m/5m/1h windows (99th percentile per minute) excluding client-side cancellations
latency_sli_p50: p50 tail measured at request completion for user-facing routes
latency_sli_p95: p95 over 1m/5m windows used for runway burn estimation
quality_sli: model-quality regression signal (eval-returned error rate) sampled per rollout
runway_model_spec: Runway windows: immediate (5m), short (1h), medium (6h). Compute burn rate over each window and project time-to-zero error budget.
Thresholds: Warning if projected TTR (time-to-ruin) < 6h; Restrict if TTR < 1h; Evacuate if TTR < 5m or observed sustained p99 latency > X ms across region.
Per-tenant runway: calculate tenant-weighted burn using token consumption and request quality importance tags.
Variant-aware projection: if a rollout increases quality_sli variance, allocate a separate runway slice for canary traffic.
Cross-region aggregation: maintain region-level runways; prefer regional restriction before global evacuation when capacity exists elsewhere.
Hysteresis: require 2 consecutive windows breaching to escalate; require runway recovery of >50% for 15m to de-escalate.
staged_actions: Notice: emit alert and create SEV-0 if enterprise tokens affected; annotate dashboards and kick off autoscale review.
Restrict: apply soft-throttle to low-priority routes, reduce max concurrent model sessions for affected variants, force degrade-to-embedding for cheap routes where acceptable.
Fallback: route traffic to cheaper compatible model variant with QoS-tagged downgrade and attach quality headers for consumer handling.
Regional Evacuate: shift non-pinned traffic away from degraded region using routing policy and prioritize capacity reservation for pinned enterprise tenants.
Emergency Kill: last-resort global shedding for non-SLA traffic if runway projection indicates imminent full breach.
circuit_breaker_spec: States: CLOSED -> WARNING -> THROTTLED -> ISOLATED -> EVACUATED
Transition triggers: runway TTR thresholds, sustained p95/p99 latency breaches, error budget burn-rate > 5x baseline over 5m
Backoff policy: exponential backoff with jitter for re-enable attempts, max retry window aligned with runway windows
Observability hooks: emit state change events to audit log, increment CB metrics, annotate trace spans with CB state
load_shedding_priority: 1. Pinned enterprise routes (never shed until forced by embargo)
2. High-quality user routes and paid features (shed last)
4. Anonymous or anonymous-low-priority tokens and fallback embeddings (preferred target for early shedding)
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: Runway projection (per-endpoint, per-region), burn-rate heatmap, CB state map, tenant exposure panel
Alerts: runway-warning (TTR < 6h), runway-critical (TTR < 1h), runway-immediate (TTR <5m) with paging and severity mapping
SLO burn notebooks: automated daily summary and ad-hoc investigation notebooks linked to ticketing
test_plan: Unit: validate SLI computation against synthetic traces
Integration: simulate 3x and 10x bursts via loadtest harness in staging across 3 regions (links below)
Chaos: kill a regional replica while running steady-state traffic and verify staged actions and evacuation sequence
Canary rollout: enable runway-enforcement for a small set of internal tenants and monitor false positives for 72h
acceptance_criteria: SLO/SLI formulas documented and reviewed by SRE + Runtime teams
Dashboard with runway projections visible in Console staging and bound to alert rules
Runtime hookpoints merged (GH PR 7891) that can accept CB state commands from policy engine
Loadtest scenario passes: system enacts Restrict and Evacuate in correct order during staged test; no pinned enterprise tokens are shed during tests
Runbook published and on-call engineers trained (docs + 1hr walkthrough recorded)
